common_patterns.overview: Common Go patterns and idioms that should be used when designing Go applications. These patterns represent best practices and established conventions in the Go community.

pattern.name: interface_based_design
pattern.description: Design around interfaces to enable loose coupling and testability. Define interfaces for behaviors that need to be abstracted.
pattern.when_to_use: When you need to decouple implementation details, enable testing with mocks, or provide multiple implementations of a behavior.

pattern.name: functional_options
pattern.description: Use functional options pattern for configurable constructors. This provides a clean API for optional parameters.
pattern.when_to_use: When constructing structs with many optional configuration parameters.

pattern.name: repository_pattern
pattern.description: Separate data access logic from business logic using repository interfaces. This makes testing easier and allows swapping storage implementations.
pattern.when_to_use: When working with databases, external APIs, or any data storage mechanism.

pattern.name: error_wrapping
pattern.description: Wrap errors with context using fmt.Errorf with %w verb to preserve the original error for error checking with errors.Is and errors.As.
pattern.when_to_use: Whenever returning an error from a function to provide additional context.

pattern.name: sentinel_errors
pattern.description: Define exported error variables for expected error conditions that callers may need to check specifically.
pattern.when_to_use: For errors that callers need to handle differently, like "not found" or "already exists".

pattern.name: worker_pool
pattern.description: Use a worker pool to limit concurrent goroutines and process work items. This prevents resource exhaustion and provides controlled concurrency.
pattern.when_to_use: When processing many tasks concurrently but need to limit resource usage.

pattern.name: context_propagation
pattern.description: Pass context.Context through your call chain to enable cancellation, timeouts, and request-scoped values.
pattern.when_to_use: For any operation that may need to be cancelled or have a timeout, especially I/O operations and long-running computations.

pattern.name: fan_out_fan_in
pattern.description: Distribute work to multiple goroutines (fan out) and collect results (fan in) for parallel processing.
pattern.when_to_use: When tasks can be processed independently and you want to speed up processing through parallelism.

pattern.name: table_driven_tests
pattern.description: Use table-driven tests for testing multiple scenarios with similar logic. This makes tests more maintainable and easier to extend.
pattern.when_to_use: When testing a function with multiple input/output combinations.

pattern.name: test_helpers
pattern.description: Create helper functions for common test setup and teardown to reduce code duplication in tests.
pattern.when_to_use: When multiple tests need similar setup or test data.
